title: Oberlin Engineering Challenge
theme: Engineering for a More Connected World
tagline: Design it. Build it. Defend it.
description: A proposed public challenge where interdisciplinary student teams could take a real problem from evidence to prototype, then explain and test important decisions before the Oberlin community.
prize_pool: Any awards or project support will be announced only after resources are confirmed

tracks.title: Robotics + Intelligent Systems
tracks.description: Machines that sense, decide, move, assist, or collaborate.

tracks.title: Climate + Community
tracks.description: Engineering responses to environmental and community needs.

tracks.title: Built World + Mechanics
tracks.description: Physical systems, structures, devices, manufacturing, and motion.

tracks.title: Open Innovation
tracks.description: Strong ideas that cross categories and create their own lane.

stages.title: Frame the problem
stages.description: Teams identify a real user, need, constraint, or system worth understanding.

stages.title: Propose the build
stages.description: Teams define scope, evidence, technical approach, milestones, and risks.

stages.title: Design reviews
stages.description: Mentors and reviewers challenge assumptions before teams invest deeply in the wrong direction.

stages.title: Build + test
stages.description: Teams iterate, document failures, measure performance, and improve the prototype.

stages.title: Public defense
stages.description: Finalists demonstrate the work and defend their choices before judges and the community.

criteria.title: Problem understanding
criteria.description: Evidence that the team understands the people, context, constraints, and stakes.

criteria.title: Engineering quality
criteria.description: Sound technical decisions, system integration, safety, rigor, and execution.

criteria.title: Testing + evidence
criteria.description: Clear metrics, thoughtful experiments, honest limitations, and learning through iteration.

criteria.title: Impact + responsibility
criteria.description: A credible path to usefulness with attention to ethics, access, cost, and consequences.

criteria.title: Communication
criteria.description: A precise explanation, compelling demonstration, and ability to defend decisions.
